readout.title: How goods moved through the chain
readout.summary: Oregon Loggers supplied cedar logs to Cedar Mill, which made slats, while Graphite Mine supplied graphite to Lead Works, which made leads. The Pencil Factory used slats and leads to make and box pencils; Pencil Shops bought a boxed pencil and sold it to a customer.

mechanisms.name: Goods made from other goods
mechanisms.explanation: Cedar Mill turned logs into slats, and Lead Works turned graphite and clay into leads. Pencil Factory then used slats and leads to make pencils and packed a pencil into a box.

mechanisms.name: Goods carried to the next step
mechanisms.explanation: Oregon Loggers sold logs to Cedar Mill, and Graphite Mine sold graphite to Lead Works. Goods also moved from Lead Works to Pencil Factory, from Cedar Mill to Pencil Factory, and from Pencil Factory to Pencil Shops.

mechanisms.name: Demand reached and met
mechanisms.explanation: Pencil Shops sold a boxed pencil to a customer, who received one pencil. This is the clearest event showing finished goods reaching and being taken by the place that wanted them.
